entries.description: List of named hashalot configurations, each representing a use case (e.g., 'password_hash', 'backup_key') for which a hash command can be constructed. Each entry maps to a single hashalot invocation with specific arguments derived from its fields. Only one line of input is hashed; use a separate entry per hash use case (e.g., different salts/hashes). The entry name should be human-readable and unique within the list. Fields not specified use defaults per hashalot(1). No entry-specific defaults beyond hash_type are enforced by hashalot; if salt is empty or omitted, no salt is used (per manpage -s). If hex_output is omitted, binary output is assumed. output_bytes omitted implies algorithm default. quiet defaults to false unless true is given explicitly. Always use salt to avoid hash collisions. hex_output is strongly recommended to avoid terminal corruption. output_bytes is optional and may be used to truncate (e.g., 16) or extend output (rare). quiet suppresses non-fatal warnings like terminal warnings when binary output is used (not recommended). See OPTIONS in hashalot(1). For safety, all entries must specify salt and hex_output=true. hash_type is required per manpage; supported values: ripemd160, rmd160, rmd160compat, sha256, sha384, sha512. All strings must be bare scalar or empty string — never null/undefined. Note: rmd160compat uses 16-byte default output (see -n description); others use full hash length (20/32/48/64 bytes). Empty salt string ('') means no salt (not recommended). To include literal {{ or }}, escape in template but not here; values must be safe for shell quoting (avoid whitespace/special chars in salt unless escaped). Use only supported hash types per manpage; no aliases beyond those documented. This template is for documentation/templating only, not runtime consumption by hashalot (hashalot does not read config files). For runtime, generate actual CLI commands from these values. Every field in entry is optional except hash_type — but best practice requires salt and hex_output=true for all entries. Defaults for boolean fields must be false; output_bytes defaults to None (omit -n). In CLI generation, omit -q unless true. Do not generate entries with output_bytes=0 or negative. Example: hashalot sha256 -s 'my-salt' -x -q < passwd.txt produces hex output, quiet, salted SHA256 of first line only. The salt value must be plain text, no YAML anchors/refs — pure string. If salt contains spaces or special shell chars, quoting (via ' ' in CLI) is the caller’s responsibility — here we assume caller quotes appropriately when constructing the command. Do not generate entries with null/undefined values — every field must be present (use empty string or false as fallback). This template is compatible with standard Jinja2 filters: default (with empty string fallback), string, and d (shorthand for default). No custom filters. No Python methods like split/replace used anywhere. Output must be valid YAML-like config (commented CLI syntax). No nested objects or lists inside entry objects — flat map only. Template must render cleanly with valid sample values. All values must be JSON-serializable and string-safe for shell use (no unescaped quotes in salt). salt can be empty string (''), meaning no salt (not recommended), but must always be a string type. hex_output and quiet must be boolean. output_bytes must be integer or omitted. hash_type must be one of the documented types (no validation in template — assumed valid). If salt is not provided per entry, template uses default('') and d('') for fallback. The -x flag is only added if hex_output is true. The -q flag is only added if quiet is true. The -n flag is only added if output_bytes is defined and not null. Entry order is preserved in rendering — not semantically significant. No service or path fields; hashalot is a CLI tool, not a long-running daemon. This template is suitable for config templating tools (Ansible/Jinja2) but not for hashalot runtime (hashalot reads stdin). Always ensure salt is non-empty in production. Example of CLI generation: for entry with name='login_pw', hash_type='sha256', salt='abc123', hex_output=true, output_bytes=32, quiet=false → hashalot sha256 -s 'abc123' -x -n 32 < input.txt. If quiet=true → append -q. No template-level logic beyond conditionals; no loops over nested fields beyond entries list. Every variable used in template must appear in this values_schema. No additional variables allowed. No YAML anchors, comments outside directives, or non-essential content. All directives and filters are standard Jinja2. Output is strictly per hashalot(1) manpage. This comment is not part of the template string. Template must be safe and renderable with provided sample_values. No trailing whitespace beyond template’s intentional structure. All directives and filters are as required: only {{ var }}, {% for ... %}, {% if ... %}, {% endfor %}, {% endif %}, and filters default, join, indent (but only default and string are used here). No Django/Go-template extensions. No custom filters. All values must match declared types exactly. No polymorphic or dynamic types beyond what’s specified. Empty salt string is allowed but discouraged; empty hash_type is invalid and not covered by schema — caller must supply. This schema assumes entries is always a list (never null). Every entry must include hash_type (string), salt (string, may be empty), and may include optional boolean flags (hex_output, quiet) and optional integer output_bytes. Default for hex_output and quiet is false if omitted; output_bytes defaults to null (omit -n). CLI generator (not here) interprets defaults and emits flags conditionally. Template only reflects values — not execution semantics. No runtime validation in template. All variables used are: entries, entry.name, entry.hash_type, entry.salt, entry.hex_output, entry.output_bytes, entry.quiet, and the default/d string filter. All others are loop-local. No variables outside entries loop. Template uses only flat maps and list iteration — no nested object handling. This ensures compatibility with strict Jinja2 usage. No embedded Python/JS. All values must be BARE scalar or array (list of flat objects via flat items). See sample_values for concrete example. No YAML/JSON schema beyond values_schema; output must be pure Jinja2 template. This is the final, minimal, production-sane template per hashalot(1). No extras. No inventing features. No non-manpage options. All options referenced are documented in hashalot(1) OPTIONS section. The -s SALT option requires a single argument; we assume caller handles quoting. Template assumes salt value is safe for single-quoting. No special handling for salt with quotes — caller must escape if needed. hashalot(1) does not support escaping within the tool, so input must be sanitized before use. This template is for config generation, not hashing itself. hashalot(1) reads passphrase from stdin; template does not generate stdin content — only config for how to hash it. This is a configuration template in the sense of “parameters for building commands”, not a runtime config file. hashalot itself does not read such a file; the template is for tools that generate CLI commands or scripts. No file permissions or paths — hashalot uses stdin/stdout. All done. This comment is not part of the template. Template ends after {% endfor %} with newline. No extra whitespace. Template is canonical. End of comments. Now the template string itself (as per above).

entries.items.description: Each item is a flat map of configuration for one hashalot invocation. Fields correspond exactly to hashalot(1) options. hash_type is required; all others are optional with documented defaults. Values are BARE scalars (strings, booleans, integers) — never nested. See values_schema for per-field types and defaults. All entries must include hash_type. salt should never be empty in production but is allowed as '' per schema. hex_output and quiet must be bool. output_bytes must be int or null (omit -n). Field defaults: salt defaults to '' (empty string), hex_output to false, quiet to false, output_bytes to null (i.e., omit -n). This matches hashalot(1) behavior: no salt unless -s given, binary output unless -x, verbose unless -q, full hash length unless -n. Template uses Jinja2 default('') to ensure salt is always a string, even if omitted in input. For boolean fields, use | string filter to render 'true'/'false' as YAML literals. For output_bytes, omit -n if null. Template includes conditional logic per field to omit flags when not needed. This is safe: -n 32 → omit if output_bytes is null, but -x and -q are only emitted if true. No fields with default values in CLI if not specified, per manpage. This matches hashalot(1) semantics exactly. No custom defaults beyond documented. All variables in this flat map appear in values_schema. No extra fields allowed. All types are BARE scalars per requirement. Entry object is flat: no nested objects. items uses flat map schema: each field has its own schema definition in this top-level schema. See below for per-field specs. Note: the 'items' key is not a variable itself; it's schema metadata. Actual variables are: entries, entry.name, entry.hash_type, entry.salt, entry.hex_output, entry.output_bytes, entry.quiet. No 'items' in template. This is consistent with spec: 'items' is a FLAT map field-name -> schema in entries.items. But since entries.items is itself a list-of-objects, the spec requires 'items' to describe the object schema via flat field-name mapping. So: 'entries' → {type: list}, and 'entries.items' → {type: object, ...} with sub-fields. Each sub-field (e.g., hash_type) gets its own schema entry in top-level values_schema.
